title: Red Giant
body:
A **red giant** is what a star becomes when the hydrogen in its core runs out.

With no fusion in the core, pressure drops and the core contracts under gravity. The
contraction heats the surrounding shell enough for hydrogen to fuse there, and that shell
produces more energy than the core ever did. The extra output pushes the outer layers far
outward, and the expansion cools them, which is why the star becomes both larger and redder
while growing more luminous.

```
the Sun today          1 solar radius,  5800 K,  luminosity 1
as a red giant         ~100 solar radii, ~3500 K, luminosity ~1000
```

On the [[HR Diagram]] the star leaves the main sequence and moves up and to the right,
which is the path the diagram's off-sequence regions record. The Sun will reach roughly the
orbit of Earth in this stage.

The core continues contracting and heating until helium fusion starts, producing carbon and
oxygen. For a low-mass star that is the last fusion stage, since the core never reaches the
temperature carbon needs. The outer layers drift away as a planetary nebula, a name given
before anyone knew what they were, and the exposed core remains as a [[White Dwarf]].
